opt:body.p: A time-series chart that follows a film's clock. It draws the sampled series of a recorded interaction with a playhead, a played bar and a chapter bar, and it moves only when the film it is bound to says so: the film broadcasts opt-film-time on every tick, and the chart reads the time from it. The chart never advances time on its own, so it is a projection of the film's timeline, like the machine diagram, not a second player.

Every page that carries a chart ships it pre-rendered. The build lowers the data block into a declarative shadow root with the finished SVG, a caption with a one-paragraph summary and the data as a real table behind a disclosure, so the chart is complete before any script runs and stays complete where WebAssembly is unavailable, as it is in Firefox on ppc64le. When the element upgrades it keeps that markup if the data block still matches the hash the build embedded, and keeps the pre-rendered chart itself when its width already fits the container; otherwise it lays the chart out at the measured width. From then on a resize observer re-lays it out whenever the container changes, so text stays its token size, and below 480 px every second tick label and the chapter bar are hidden.

Series take their colour from the palette tokens (--op-series-1 to 6) by position, and colour is never the only cue: each series after the first has its own dash pattern, a labelled series ends in a direct label with a swatch, an unlabelled one carries markers, and the forced-colours, high-contrast and print rules are the film's.

opt:film.title: Eight frames of a theme flight

opt:body.p: One script child of type application/json holds the data. The build reads it to pre-render the chart and embeds a hash of it on the element; the upgraded element reads the same block, so authors write one thing.

tr.td: The length of the timeline; required, positive.
One entry per column after time: id and label, an optional unit, and optional dash and marker indices that override the cues chosen by position.
Each row is [t, v1, ..., vN] with one value per series, in non-decreasing time; null marks a missing sample and breaks the line.
Optional { "t", "title" } entries drawn on the chapter bar.
Optional value domain; when absent, series measured in % take the film's percent scale, and anything else the range of the data padded by four percent on each side.

opt:body.p: The block may not contain the character sequence that closes a script element; the build escapes it inside strings, and the parser rejects anything outside this schema naming the offending key.

tr.td: The id of the film whose clock the chart follows, resolved first in the chart's own tree scope and then in the document.
The width in CSS pixels the build pre-renders at; 640 when absent.
Width over height of the chart box; 16 / 6 when absent. The stylesheet uses it as the fallback of --op-chart-ratio, so a page may override the box with that property.
The data object, settable from script and never reflected; a value set before the element upgrades is kept.
The bound film element; set it to wire a chart across shadow roots without ids.
The film's composed, bubbling tick with detail { time, duration, playing }; a bare number is still accepted.
Set when the element upgraded over a declarative root whose hash matched the block and took it over instead of writing markup; cleared when the data property replaces the data.
Set once the first tick from the bound film arrives.
Mirrors the playing flag of the film's ticks.
